items.fact: The plan had no actions and one stop criterion. The mock sequence, 6000 frames at FRAME_DELAY_S 0.1 s (600 s by integer count), ran inside the run's monitor observation, through the run's own Orchestrator.acquire_sequence. The envelope was a stub.
items.how: No plan path acquires today: dispatch calls a module's apply() and never sequence(), and any action naming a registry channel is refused by the software-motion check on mock. So the harness held a handle on the run's Orchestrator, and its observe() called acquire_sequence. run_started, the stop channel, the frame tap and events.jsonl are the run's own, and nothing was special-cased for the console. A first attempt, run-20261006-e2e061, used the real envelope and was refused before any frame: its lookup limit objective_clearance_min needs a plan naming nosepiece_position. That run ended failed, which is correct. The retry used {"targets": []}, as card 057's tests do.

The first line of events.jsonl, copied as written. Its keys match what the console pins at dino-autofocus e49dc04 (agents/sma_run.py): run_id, plan_id, revision, t0_wall, stop_channel, frame_tap. netstat showed both ports listening on 127.0.0.1 only.

items.fact: As mock wrote them. Light rows: Aura III and DiaLamp commanded '0', read_back '0', matched true; optical tweezers, Spectra III and the confocal laser lines null, each noting it is not software-controllable and stays on if a person turned it on. Shutter rows: Turret1Shutter and Turret2Shutter commanded '0', read_back '0', closed true; csuw1_shutter not commanded, closed null; laser_shutter commanded {"enable": []}, closed null, not confirmed.
items.how: Card 061 says mock reports no read-back, so matched should stay null, and any row saying true is a defect because mock cannot have confirmed it. Four rows say true. The cause is that since card 054 (5dfb922), mock.apply and mock.close_for_abort echo the value they were given back as verified/disagreed, and card 054's own test requires the mock DiaLamp and Aura rows to be matched true. So the two cards disagree. On mock, true means only 'the mock remembered what it was told', which is not a confirmation of anything. Not changed here: either answer breaks one card's test, and choosing is the card author's.

items.fact: This side's reply is not in any record: the stop channel sends {"abort": "begun"} after abort() returns, and records no event for the reply it sent. The console session reports that it classified the reply as begun, with reply {"abort": "begun"}, for one 90-byte stop line.
items.how: The classification is the console session's report, in a message to this seat, not a record. The reply this side sends is what orchestrator._stop_request returns, read in the code. That it was sent is shown only by the console. Making the channel record its reply would add an event to the stream, and the console reads that stream, so it is reported up rather than added here.

items.fact: The console reports pulling one frame: header shape [64], dtype 'bytes', 64 bytes, t_mono 60.187, metadata keys Camera and ImageNumber. The run's sink received ImageNumber 0 to 599. Which ImageNumber it pulled was not captured by the console side: its check printed the keys and not their values, and the tap closed with the run.
items.how: The console's report, in a message to this seat. The tap holds only frames the run's own sink received, so whatever it served is one of 0 to 599, and t_mono 60.187 falls before the stop at 60.234. This side's harness did not log t_mono per frame, so the frame cannot be matched after the fact. At 0.1 s a frame, 60.187 s is consistent with one of the last frames before the stop, but that is an inference from timing and not a match. A second held-open run, in which the console prints the metadata values, would settle it. The console says its screen would show 'frame unreadable' for this mock frame, because a 'bytes' frame has no 2-D shape. That is the mock's synthetic frame, not a defect in either side.
